questions.q: Which tool is best suited for a smaller, one-time, or exploratory migration from SQL Server into Cosmos DB?
options: The Azure Cosmos DB Data Migration Tool
Neo4j LOAD CSV
SQL Server Reporting Services
The Cosmos DB change feed
questions.explain: The free, open-source Data Migration Tool is purpose-built for smaller or exploratory moves, supporting SQL Server, JSON, CSV, and MongoDB among its sources.

questions.q: Which tool is the right choice for a production-grade, large-scale, or ongoing migration into Cosmos DB?
options: Azure Data Factory
MongoDB Compass
Neo4j Desktop
Azure Monitor
questions.explain: ADF has native Cosmos DB connectors plus the mapping data flows, scheduling, and monitoring a real production migration pipeline needs.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the single most common mistake teams make when migrating from SQL Server to Cosmos DB?
options: Migrating each normalized table into its own container unchanged, without redesigning for embed/reference patterns and partition keys
Using Azure Data Factory instead of the Data Migration Tool
Choosing too high a consistency level
Forgetting to enable the change feed before migrating
questions.explain: A straight lift-and-shift of a normalized schema usually produces a database that performs and costs worse than the one it replaced.

questions.q: Why does a query that was a simple JOIN in SQL Server become expensive after an unchanged lift-and-shift into Cosmos DB?
options: Cosmos DB has no server-side JOIN across containers, so the app must make multiple round trips, each costing its own RUs
Cosmos DB queries are always slower than SQL Server regardless of design
JOINs are not supported in any NoSQL database, including MongoDB and Neo4j
The migration tools corrupt the data during transfer
questions.explain: Without a server-side JOIN, the application has to stitch multiple container reads together in code, and each read is its own billed RU cost.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend using as the default partition key when redesigning a migrated container, instead of just reusing the old SQL Server primary key?
options: Whatever value matches the dominant access pattern for that data in its new shape
Always the same value across every container for consistency
A randomly generated GUID with no relation to the data
The name of the original SQL Server table
questions.explain: The partition key should be chosen to match how the data will actually be queried in Cosmos DB, not carried over by default from the relational primary key.
